title: Whether ‘this is God’s word’ is an act of faith — mere logomachy
source_text: XXIX. Porro ad tollendam hanc difficultatem, nihil attinet quaerere an judicium illud, quo statuimus revelationem, quae nobis proponitur, & per quam nobis credenda confirmantur, vere divinam esse, fidei actus sit, & dici debeat: an vero judicium quoddam fidem praecedens, & ab ea praerequisitum, quod ex Theologis alii affirmant, alii vero negant. Sed haec vere est mera λογομαχία. Nam prout libebit fidei definitionem restringere, vel ampliare, sic quoque actus ille vel fidei includetur, vel ab ea excludetur. Etenim, si quis fidem definiat assensum quo aliquid verum esse statuimus, propter Dei dicentis authoritatem & testimonium, tum judicium istud non est actus fidei, sed tantum aliquid quod fidem necessario antecedit, & ab ea praesupponitur. Nam testimonium illud, quod reliquorum omnium credendorum argumentum est, non creditur propter aliud testimonium divinum, cujus authoritate mens nostra moveatur: nisi quis hic velit admittere circulum, aut progressum in infinitum, quorum utrumque absurdum est, ut ante observatum fuit. Si quis autem fidem definiat assensum illum quo verbum divinum ut tale suscipimus, & propter illud assentimur omnibus quae nobis in eo credenda proponuntur; tum assignandi erunt duo fidei actus, quorum prior erit judicium illud quo statuimus hoc verbum vere divinum esse, alter vero assensus quem praebemus omnibus quae illo continentur. Utcunque vero de eo sit, sive judicium istud dicatur actus fidei, sive non, profecto, si sumus incerti an revelatio quae nobis proponitur divina sit, non possumus propter eam certum assensum praebere illis quae nobis ejus authoritate commendantur.
pass_a_gloss: Further, to remove this difficulty it does not avail to ask whether that judgment by which we lay down that the revelation proposed to us, and by which things to be believed are confirmed to us, is truly divine, is and ought to be called an act of faith; or whether it is a certain judgment preceding faith and prerequisite to it — which some Theologians affirm and others deny. But this truly is mere logomachy. For according as it shall please to restrict or enlarge the definition of faith, so also that act will be included in faith or excluded from it. For if anyone define faith as the assent by which we lay down that something is true because of the authority and testimony of God speaking, then that judgment is not an act of faith, but only something which necessarily precedes faith and is presupposed by it. For that testimony which is the argument of all the remaining things to be believed is not believed because of another divine testimony by whose authority our mind is moved — unless someone here wish to admit a circle or a progress to infinity, both of which are absurd, as was observed before. But if anyone define faith as that assent by which we receive the divine word as such, and because of it assent to all things proposed to us in it to be believed, then two acts of faith will have to be assigned, of which the former will be that judgment by which we lay down that this word is truly divine, the latter the assent we afford to all things contained in it. But however it be — whether that judgment be called an act of faith or not — assuredly, if we are uncertain whether the revelation proposed to us is divine, we cannot because of it afford certain assent to those things commended to us by its authority.
pass_b_english: ‘Is this-God’s-word an act of faith?’ = λογομαχία (definition stretch).
Narrow faith-def: judgment precedes faith (else circle/regress).
Wide faith-def: two acts — word-is-divine + assent to contents.
Either way: uncertain revelation → no certain assent on its authority.

choices.why: Dismisses act-of-faith labeling as the fix.
rejected: settling the act-of-faith label removes the certainty difficulty
